Reverted main.cpp to version from master

This code looks identical to the code in lines 74-81. Would it make sense to move this to a new private method to avoid duplication? It seems prone to errors in the future if someone changes one of these and forgets to change the other one.
Moved the zone creation to its own method. This also helps avoid the extra query of the Available property below.
Not a big deal, but this queries the value of Available again. If you refactor the zone creation into a private method, maybe that can be avoided. Same comment for availIfaceAdded().
With the zone creation in its own method, these init calls can just be switched to create the zones instead, which avoids the extra query.
Just curious - why does this have 'Holder' in the name?
Since there's just the one variable for now, this map isn't really needed, and can be replaced with a hard-coded constant in the header file.

This code is mostly duplicated 3 times in this file. Seems like a candidate for common code function.

Rather than hardcoding this loop and looking for specific variable name holders (?), could you do the following:
* Create a chassis-specific variables map with key/value pairs that are the variable names and values. e.g. `{"$chassis", "3"}`.
* Create a method that takes as input a string that can contain variables and the variables map.
  * Loop over all the variables in the map
    * Replace any instances of the variable name (map key) with the variable value (map value) within the current string.

See the following function in phosphor-power which does this: https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-power/blob/master/json_parser_utils.cpp#L215
The _jsonVars loop and if check probably aren't needed here, especially now that that _jsonVars map is replaced with a hard-coded constant. Just the expandVar call should be enough.
Should these be const references? Does it make sense to make a const copy of something? Maybe it is needed due to the way other code works.

Matt mentioned in another review that it would be better to pass by const reference. Probably just so that it doesn't create a copy https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-fan-presence/+/87787/comment/10b6a357_ef1aaac4/

I agree with Matt; that was my comment.

Currently you are passing just as a const, not a const reference. So it is making a copy, and then declaring the copy const (which doesn't really matter).
Think I just left off the & for the reference by mistake. Added that in
This name is confusing (to me). Is it a chassis number? Or a reference to something else that has the chassis number?

It's meant to be a chassis number for the chassis that the struct represents. The way the JSON is structured, a single chassis configuration can apply across multiple different chassis via a chassis_numbers list in the JSON file. So I was storing this chassis numbers list alongside a reference to the specific chassis that the struct is being used to configure in code. I didn't find much use for the chassis numbers list in the Chassis/MultiChassisSystem class logic, though, so I decided to remove it, which is shown in the diff.

I guess my comment was would it make more sense to just call this chassisNumber or just number (since we are already in a chassis struct)?

If not that is OK. Just trying to understanding the naming.
Yeah, `chassisNum` for the name probably makes more sense.
unintended change?
Yeah, I think the white space removal got left there from when I made changes to fan.cpp. I'll add that back in
